headline: President Trump has created a White House task force called the Super Intelligence Force and put the director of national intelligence, Jay Clayton, in charge of coordinating US AI policy.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a new federal body announced by the president, with named members and reporting lines.
importance_line: Changes who speaks for the US government on AI, affecting the public and AI companies, but the group's powers are not stated and Trump has ruled out regulating the industry.
summary: NBC News reports that Trump announced the task force on Sunday 4 Oct on Truth Social, with Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson and Defense Undersecretary Emil Michael as other members; it reports to Trump and chief of staff Susie Wiles. It follows NBC's report on Friday that Clayton was expected to become AI czar, and last week's White House meeting with tech leaders, after which Trump spoke of a nonbinding deal of "tremendous self-regulation".
notes: Follow-up to yesterday's story: today's new fact is the formal announcement, the leader and members. Article read in full.
